headlines.headline: Futures drift lower into the open: Dow -308 pts (-0.58%), S&P 500 -15.5 pts (-0.2%), Nasdaq 100 roughly flat (Reuters, ~06:09 ET). Caution prevails after the AI-led rout; Brent near a five-month high adds inflation worry ahead of next week's FOMC meeting.
headlines.why_it_matters: Another stabilization attempt at thin levels - watch whether the Nasdaq's flat line holds or fades into the opening auction; the Dow's red tone is the SpaceX telecom shock bleeding into index futures.

headlines.headline: SpaceX telecom report hits carriers: Bloomberg (unnamed sources) says SpaceX is in talks with at least one major cellular-infrastructure company, including Crown Castle, for access to a minimum of 80,000 U.S. cell sites to build a fourth nationwide wireless carrier. Premarket: TMUS -4.3%, VZ -3.7%, T -3.3%; CCI +6.5-9%, AMT +4-5%; Deutsche Telekom -3.1%, Vodafone and Orange ~-1.5% in Europe; SpaceX +2% premarket. TD Cowen estimates a nationwide terrestrial buildout would cost $80B+; 80,000 sites is ~half of the 158,500 U.S. towers (Wireless Infrastructure Association).
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed - SpaceX didn't respond to comment and CCI's CEO gave a non-denial ('talking to all parties'). If confirmed, it re-prices U.S. wireless from oligopoly to open warfare; the tower operators are the clear winners either way, which is why CCI/AMT ripped.

headlines.headline: Meta details flesh out the funding story: Q3 revenue $64.60B (+26%, beat), GAAP EPS $3.83 vs $7.40 adjusted excluding a $9.89B legal charge (52-state teen-mental-health settlement); Q3 capex $34.91B exceeded operating cash flow $32.79B, flipping FCF to -$2.12B (first ever, vs +$10.63B a year ago); spreads on Meta's 5-year credit default swaps hit all-time highs; board approved a 1:1 distribution of nonvoting Class C shares in Jan 2027 (future fundraising currency, preserving Zuckerberg control); Q4 revenue guide $73-76B; New Mexico's $25B penalty accrual, Meta intends to appeal. Shares closed -6.98% at $648.85 on 40.6M shares (+91% above 30-day avg); premarket $646.85 (-0.31%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The pricing question has fully flipped from 'what AI earns' to 'who pays for AI' - CDS at record highs means creditors, not just equity, are repricing the $825B commitment load ($355.7B data-center leases + $454.5B cloud contracts). Every AI-infra name (CRWV, LRCX, AMAT) trades off this tape.

headlines.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang told CNBC capital availability is becoming a challenge for the AI infrastructure industry, with demand exceeding available funding; Ed Yardeni called the AI trade a bubble but argued moderating valuations could benefit markets without threatening the broader economy (IC Markets recap).
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source (IC recap of CNBC), but it corroborates the Meta thesis from the buy side: even AI's biggest supplier concedes the constraint is now money, not chips. That is the macro frame every headline today trades against.

headlines.headline: TSLA trades +0.17% premarket at $375.22 after closing Thursday -3.08% at $374.58; the Mag 7 weekly wrap shows Tesla owned the best week (+~5% into Thursday) on its Q3 FCF surprise while META was the worst (-~5%); AAPL remains the YTD leader at ~+27% and is the only Mag 7 name up this month on its AI-light positioning.
headlines.why_it_matters: Tesla is the one megacap whose cash-flow print bought it goodwill - it's the counter-template to Meta's 'growth now, pay later' repricing. Premarket green vs red peers shows relative strength holding into the open.

headlines.headline: Oil is the morning's pressure point: WTI $101.03 (+1.57%), Brent $113.6-114.3 (+0.4-0.7%) near five-month highs on Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure plus reports of US-Israel attack planning on Iran (the latter single-source, unconfirmed). The 10Y sits 4.96-4.98% after Thursday's biggest one-day drop in 3+ years.
headlines.why_it_matters: Confirmed crude bid vs fragile war headlines: the oil price is real, the attack-planning report is not. $100+ crude plus sticky 10Y is the stagflation shadow over every rally attempt this morning.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news this morning. Carried: Q3 cash distribution $0.525 per common unit ($2.10 annualized, ~8.4% yield) payable Nov 6 to holders of record Oct 26; Q3 earnings release before the open Tue Nov 3 with a 11 AM ET call; Q2 beat (EPS $0.31 vs $0.28 est, revenue $342.15M); now listed on the Texas Stock Exchange; Oct 1 internal reorg issued 34.47M non-convertible 9.25% Class A units to subsidiary J-W Energy.

Telecom open: whether T, VZ, TMUS stabilize or keep sliding on the unconfirmed SpaceX report; CCI/AMT the other side of the pair.

Futures into the auction: Nasdaq futures flat-to-green; SPY 760.85 / QQQ 699.10 levels from Friday outlooks. Semis after WDC's beat-and-raise traded down 4.4% after hours - MU, SNDK, STX take the cue from memory.
FOMC Oct 27-28 next week; GOOGL/MSFT/AMZN report Oct 28 - the capex-funding question gets its biggest airing then.
analysis: What changed since the 4:00 AM PT brief: the overnight headline is the Bloomberg SpaceX telecom report (single-source, unconfirmed) - it gave the tape a new sector story (carriers down 3-4% premarket, towers up) that the thin futures (Dow -0.58%, S&P -0.2%) are partly absorbing. The Meta story deepened from one fact ($825B commitments, -$2.12B FCF) into a funding dossier: record CDS spreads, a Class C issuance currency, a $25B New Mexico penalty accrual, and a raised 2026 capex floor ($135-145B) that rises every quarter. Huang's CNBC comment independently validates the frame: the AI constraint is now capital, not demand. Signal vs noise: the crude bid (WTI $101) and CDS repricing are signal; the SpaceX report, the Iran strike planning, and the Anthropic S-1 timing are all single-source noise until confirmed. The market's shape is unchanged from 4am: crowded-AI deleveraging with defensive rotation, not a broad collapse - AAPL flat, TSLA green, Dow holding up. The opening auction will test whether the telecom shock is contained or contagious.
